label: WardStock - Medications InfluxDB Cleanup (ONE-OFF)
info:
Aug 23 2026, one-off (Ward: "clean up the old duplicate 2025-08-12 points"). Not a recurring
flow — run it once, then it's safe to leave disabled or delete the tab entirely.

Background: godaddy_pull_flow.json used to timestamp every 'medications' point at noon,
server-local time. Fixed today (Aug 23) to anchor at midnight UTC instead — see that flow's
tab info for the full story. But every medication that existed before today's fix now has
TWO points in InfluxDB for the same dosage era: an old one at the legacy noon-local time and
a fresh one at midnight UTC written by the fixed code on the next pull. Not just Duloxetine —
since 'medications' is always pulled in FULL on every run (never a delta), every currently-
tracked medication picked up a duplicate the moment the fix landed.

Why 'delete everything and re-pull' instead of surgically deleting just the old points: the
old points aren't all at exactly the same time-of-day. Noon Eastern is 16:00 UTC in EDT but
17:00 UTC in EST, so a precise deletion would need to know exactly which historical dates fell
on which side of the DST boundary — fragile and easy to get subtly wrong. Wiping the whole
'medications' measurement and immediately re-pulling is safe specifically BECAUSE that
measurement is always a full, complete refresh from GoDaddy's MySQL database (the actual
source of truth) on every single pull — nothing here is unique to InfluxDB or would be lost.

Does NOT touch 'medication_dosage_history' — checked first (see n_mic_check_history_exec):
that measurement doesn't exist in the bucket yet (the one dosage-change save that would have
populated it hit the medication_dosage_history INSERT failure investigated earlier today), so
there's nothing there to clean up, and it isn't safe to blanket-delete the same way anyway
(it's populated via since_last delta pulls, not a full refresh — wiping it could lose history
a simple re-pull wouldn't bring back).

Steps: check for a waiting import (skipped, this flow doesn't do that) -- N/A, this flow only
has two real steps: (1) InfluxDB v2 delete API call scoped to _measurement="medications" across
all time, (2) dynamic Link Call into godaddy_pull_flow.json's entry point to immediately
repopulate clean points. Logged under job_name=medications_influx_cleanup in sync_job_runs for
the same traceability every other job gets, even though it's not meant to run again.

UNTESTED, same caveat as everything else — this is also the first use of InfluxDB's DELETE API
in this project (every other flow only ever writes or, as of wherewhen_data_export_flow.json,
queries). Worth double-checking the delete actually returned 204 before trusting the re-pull
step ran against a truly empty measurement.

name: Manual trigger — DELETES DATA, run once deliberately
Load secrets + start job log
Prepare InfluxDB delete request (measurement=medications)
Check delete response (expect 204)
Re-pull GoDaddy to repopulate clean points
Log success
Log failure
Prepare finish-point write
SQLite: ensure job_status table exists
sqlite: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
SQLite: prep status UPSERT
